insights.title: Kemps Corner: Performance History and Insights
insights.subtitle: Kwality House, Kemps Corner · Nov-2024 to Oct-2026 · Prepared Nov-2026 · Document 1 of 3 for this studio

intro.text: Kemps Corner earned ₹329.4L in the 12 months to Oct-2026, up 18.0% on the year before (₹279.1L). Renewals carry the studio (55% of revenue), April is its biggest month, and the September 2026 price increase has already lifted the average renewal ticket. The weak spots are discount creep, weekend first visits that rarely convert, and hosted classes that bring footfall but not members.

blocks.lead: Growth came from more clients, not just higher prices.
blocks.text: 1,176 people bought in the last 12 months, up from 961 (+22%). New-client revenue grew to ₹81.2L and reactivations to ₹30.3L.

blocks.lead: April 2026 was a record ₹50.0L, but it was bought with discount.
blocks.text: Average discount in April 2026 was 30.1% against 14.1% in April 2025. Codes such as ANN-2026-25%-KH ran at 47.7% effective discount. 57% of April 2026 buyers bought again by October.
Discounts were 17.3% of gross sales in the last 12 months against 9.3% the year before. The 10% pack code ZAP10 alone carried ₹36.3L of sales.

1-Month Unlimited moved from ₹18,637.50 to ₹20,238.75 (+8.6%), the 12-class pack from ₹15,802.50 to ₹19,687.50 (+24.6%) and the 8-class pack from ₹10,710 to ₹13,125 (+22.5%). September and October 2026 still delivered ₹29.1L and ₹36.1L, so demand absorbed the increase.

blocks.lead: Hosted classes create visits, not members.
blocks.text: 330 first visits came through hosted classes and only 4.2% bought. Regular trial classes converted at 34.3% and paid first visits at 43.9%.
Saturday first visits converted at 17.8% and Sunday at 19.9%, against 38.9% on Wednesday and 35.5% on Tuesday. Weekends carry 586 of 1147 first visits.

blocks.lead: Members who use their pack renew; members who don't, leave.
blocks.text: Only 30% of clients who used under a quarter of their sessions renewed, against 81% of those who used three quarters or more. 3-Month Unlimited renews at 90%; the 4-class pack at 58%.

blocks.lead: Strength Lab is full; Cardio Barre Express is empty.
blocks.text: Strength Lab classes run at 66–85% fill against 45.6% for the studio. Cardio Barre Express averages 4.3 clients (22.6% fill) and 4 pm classes 23.7% fill.

Revenue includes 5% GST. Paying clients = unique buyers in the month. Visits = class check-ins (paid check-ins exclude complimentary visits). Same calendar months sit next to each other; Sep and Oct appear for both 2025 and 2026.

74.7% of memberships and packs that ended between Nov-2025 and Sep-2026 were renewed (1,112 products). 234 members whose product ended in Nov-2025 to Aug-2026 have not come back: this is the core winback list for 2027.

under 25%

blocks.text: 4,160 classes ran with 57,874 spots; 26,409 check-ins gives a 45.6% fill rate (6.3 clients per class). 127 classes had no check-ins. Late cancellations were 10.5% of bookings.
Trainers with 10+ first-time clients, Nov-2025 to Oct-2026 (Teacher Payroll stats).
12.6% of revenue has no 'Sold By' recorded.
Clients buy at the start of the week: Monday (19.9%) and Thursday (18.4%) are the biggest sales days; Sunday is 6.6%.
36.9% of revenue lands in the last 10 days of the month, when expiring members renew. The first week carries only 17.4%.
Members average 8.2 sessions a month; 42% of members who ended a product had used a freeze.
Converters decide fast: of 1147 first visits, 153 bought within a week and 65 in days 8–30. After 30 days the chance drops sharply.
Privates are a ₹20.3L business at Kemps Corner (10-session packs and single sessions), sold at a 59% average discount on the Studio Private Class line.

blocks.text: Each line is sized on the last 12 months of this studio's own data. The lines overlap partly and should not be added together.

Protect price. The September 2026 increase held; the risk now is giving it back through codes. Every campaign offer stays within 25% effective discount and replaces, never stacks on, the standing perks.
Sell usage, not just packs. Renewal rates track session use, so the first 30 days of every membership need a visit plan (book the next 3 classes at the point of sale, trainer check-in at visit 4).
Move trials to weekdays. Offer weekday trial slots first when a lead books; keep weekend trials for leads who cannot do weekdays.
Turn hosted classes into a sales event: every hosted class needs a lead capture, an on-the-spot offer that expires in 72 hours, and a named follow-up owner.
Price Strength Lab as scarce. It is the fullest format and cannot be offered free; use it as the reward for longer commitments rather than a trial product.
Use April for higher-value purchases (3M, 6M, Annual) with value-adds, not deep percentage cuts, and plan May to bring April buyers back.
Source files: Sales – Raw – Sales (to 5-Nov-2026), Lead Data, New Visitors & Conversions, Lapsed & Renewals, Session Performance Data, Teacher Payroll stats, Meta Leads, Pricing – Mumbai / Bengaluru.
The 12-month base is Nov-2025 to Oct-2026; the prior year is Nov-2024 to Oct-2025.
Trial attendance (no-shows) is not recorded, so lead → trial uses completed trials only.
Meta ad data covers late July to early November 2026 only; Google Ads spend is not in the files.

First-visit conversion (New Visitors file) and lead conversion (Lead Data) are measured on different populations and do not add up to the same totals; the 2027 targets use volume ratios that reconcile with actual sales.
Reactivation outreach is not logged, so response rates to winback messages cannot be measured yet.

blocks.lead: Split each month into four revenue streams.
blocks.text: Renewals, reactivations and add-ons are planned from the studio's own run-rate plus realistic improvement; new-client revenue is what remains. Each stream is then divided by the average spend to give the number of clients needed.

New-client revenue has to grow 36% to reach ₹35 lakh a month: part price (+12% ticket), part volume (338 new members against 278 last year).

insights.subtitle: Supreme HQ, Bandra · Nov-2024 to Oct-2026 · Prepared Nov-2026 · Document 1 of 3 for this studio

intro.text: Bandra earned ₹201.5L in the 12 months to Oct-2026, flat on the year before (₹202.3L, -0.4%). Renewals grew, but new-client revenue fell from ₹79.1L to ₹56.6L. Leads are plentiful; too few become members, and the paid-website leads barely convert.

blocks.text: It dropped from ₹79.1L to ₹56.6L while renewals rose to ₹116.5L (+13%) and reactivations to ₹17.8L (+67%).

blocks.lead: Leads are not the problem; conversion is.
blocks.text: Bandra created 2,380 leads, more than Kemps Corner, but only 12.3% became buyers against 18.9% at Kemps Corner. First visits convert at 19.5%.

blocks.lead: Paid-website leads are the weakest source.
blocks.text: 691 'Website' leads (Google and Meta ads) reached a trial 17.8% of the time and bought 5.1% of the time. Meta spend from late July to early November 2026 was ₹1,27,908 for 205 leads (₹624 per lead).
Client referrals reached a trial 86% of the time; WhatsApp enquiries bought 28.5% of the time and phone enquiries 28.1%.

blocks.lead: The Newcomers 2-for-1 sells but does not convert.
blocks.text: It sold 384 times (₹7.0L), yet Bandra's new members were only 219.
April 2026 delivered ₹27.4L against ₹28.5L in April 2025, even though average discount rose from 13.1% to 25.3%.

blocks.text: 6 pm classes ran at 33.1% fill across 547 classes; Cardio Barre at 29.5%. FIT runs at 67.1%.
Conversion by associate cannot be managed without attribution.

blocks.text: 3,070 leads (the most of any studio) but 35.3% reached a trial and 12.6% bought. Only 133 new clients bought a membership or pack in the year.

blocks.lead: Paid-website leads do not reach the studio.

'Client unresponsive' and 'did not answer' stages cover 41% of leads; 'proximity' closes another 9.9%.

blocks.lead: Hosted and outdoor events add visits, not members.
blocks.text: 459 hosted first visits converted at 3.5% and outdoor-class leads at 0.9%. Saturday first visits (549) converted at 10.2%, Monday at 40.9%.
78.7% of memberships and packs that ended were renewed; 3-Month Unlimited renews at 88% and 1-Month Unlimited at 84%.

blocks.lead: Kenkere is the least discount-dependent studio.
blocks.text: Discounts were 7.2% of gross sales. The one deep code, VDAY50! (38 sales at 39% off), showed that a sharp, time-boxed offer can move volume.

Each month keeps its share of the last 12 months, so every month grows by the same rate and the seasonal shape (strong April and October, softer February–March and November) is preserved.

blocks.lead: Split each month into four revenue streams.
blocks.text: Renewals, reactivations and add-ons are planned from the studio's own run-rate plus realistic improvement; new-client revenue is what remains. Each stream is then divided by the average spend to give the number of clients needed.
New members ÷ conversion rate gives first visits; first visits ÷ show-up rate gives leads. Renewal revenue ÷ renewal ticket gives renewals; reactivation revenue ÷ comeback purchase gives winbacks.
The plan needs about 30% more visits than last year, which takes fill from 24.1% to 31.4%.
The pop-ups grow +30%: new-client revenue +23% (551 new paying clients), repeat pack purchases double to ₹3,13,534, and add-on drop-ins grow +20%.
